videos.title: (HSMA 6 Day 7) 2A Introduction to Discrete Event Simulation
videos.description:
Today we begin module 2 of the programme, in which we explore how we can model pathway and queuing problems using a modelling method known as Discrete Event Simulation.  We'll explore how Discrete Event Simulations work and you'll have a chance to design your own. 

GitHub (2A): https://github.com/hsma-programme/h6_2a_intro_to_des

Slides (2A): https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1HO0wXTocHRZgeuLadkGvqf5yC8BEmQzTcgo8QHOd0yY/edit?usp=sharing

HSMA Website : https://sites.google.com/nihr.ac.uk/hsma

videos.title: (HSMA 6 Day 7) 2B SimPy Part 1
videos.description:
Today we look at how we can use the SimPy Python package (which is built around generator functions) to build Discrete Event Simulations in Python.

GitHub (2B): https://github.com/hsma-programme/h6_simpy_part_1/tree/main

Slides (2B): https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/15bQX0yxfDgjNVJSQORNzBCWVvbKI_LaTcbtYVKsvYcU/edit?usp=sharing

HSMA Website : https://sites.google.com/nihr.ac.uk/hsma

videos.title: (HSMA 6 Day 8) 2C SimPy Part 2
videos.description:
In this session we look at some more advanced DES concepts and how we can incorporate them in our SimPy models.  This includes warm up periods, priority-based queuing, resource unavailability, Lognormal distributions, reneging, balking and jockeying.

Slides : https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1y7S7bjJtdLQCquzzZ2vjYzRx9-RwXE-SWgWf88fLc4o/edit?usp=sharing

GitHub : https://github.com/hsma-programme/h6_simpy_part_2

(HSMA 6 Day 10) 3D - Location Allocation Problems
videos.description:
In this session we talk about how to construct and carry out the p-median location allocation problem - minimising a weighted cost across a region for different possible combinations of sites. 

Materials can be found here: https://github.com/hsma-programme/h6_3d_facility_location_problems

videos.title: (HSMA 6 Day 10) 3C - A brief introduction to routingpy
videos.description:
In this video we briefly talk about the routingpy library and introduce how it could be used to retrieve travel matrices and isochrone data to assist in p-median location allocation problems and more.

All materials for this session can be found here: https://github.com/hsma-programme/h6_3c_interactive_plots_travel

videos.title: (HSMA 6 Day 10) 4A  - Introduction to AI and Machine Learning
videos.description:
In this session we introduce some of the core concepts of AI and Machine Learning, including the concepts of features and labels, overfitting and underfitting and assessing model performance.  We also explore some of the different types of machine learning, and practice our understanding of these new concepts by seeing if we can unpick patterns in Dan's film preferences for "Dan's Desert Island DVDs".

Slides : https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1EcO71B5kEvaSkvKQeGnuO2g4Ss4RKhrphR3gE8vv-Gk/edit?usp=sharing

HSMA Website : https://sites.google.com/nihr.ac.uk/hsma

videos.title: (HSMA 6 Day 11) 4B - Logistic Regression - Who Would Survive the Titanic?
videos.description:
In this session we'll begin exploring some of the Machine Learning approaches that we can use, starting today with Logistic Regression - a way of fusing together traditional linear regression models with a logistic function to create a powerful classifier model.  You'll see how these models can be implemented in Python, and practice using both the Titanic dataset you saw earlier in the course, as well as a new stroke patient dataset.

Slides : https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1MdLRe4-089MsEWttK9OgFvgBX8EqJ6LFCRC72zyz1jI/edit?usp=sharing

HSMA Website : https://sites.google.com/nihr.ac.uk/hsma

videos.title: (HSMA 6 Day 11) 4C  - Ethics in AI
videos.description:
In this session we'll explore some of the key ethical considerations that are fundamental to any machine learning work, as we explore what can (and will) go wrong.

Slides : https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/16Qwx0cUdGjtqqD7WQ-4kAWHBdJvBFHMch_AwPUwrp1M/edit?usp=sharing

HSMA Website : https://sites.google.com/nihr.ac.uk/hsma

videos.title: (HSMA 6 Day 12) 4D Part 1/2 - Decision Trees
videos.description:
In this session we'll begin looking at how decision trees are built and how we can use the sklearn implementation of decision trees on our own datasets.

We also recap sensitivity (recall), specificity and precision and how to calculate these in sklearn.

Slides : https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1LgVvgLzm4dxCdDCusjWWC_SBrtXhhCPchHXK4oI0kWU/edit?usp=sharing

Repository: https://github.com/hsma-programme/h6_4d_decision_trees_random_forests

HSMA Website : https://sites.google.com/nihr.ac.uk/hsma

videos.title: (HSMA 6 Day 12) 4D Part 2/2 - Random Forests, F1 score + Confusion Matrices
videos.description:
In this session we'll take a look at how we can avoid some of the problems of decision trees by using an ensemble method - random forests.

We also find out an easier way of calculating sensitivity, specificity and precision in one function, as well as hearing about a new metric called f1 score, and we learn about the confusion matrix, which is a powerful tool for helping to break down how different models perform. 

Slides : https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1LgVvgLzm4dxCdDCusjWWC_SBrtXhhCPchHXK4oI0kWU/edit?usp=sharing

Repository: https://github.com/hsma-programme/h6_4d_decision_trees_random_forests

HSMA Website : https://sites.google.com/nihr.ac.uk/hsma

videos.title: (HSMA 6 Day 12) 4E Part 1/2 - Boosting Trees for Classification Problems
videos.description:
In this session we'll take a look at a family of models called boosted trees.
These are a very powerful type of algorithm that perform extremely well on tabular datasets.
The session touches on XGBoost, AdaBoost, CatBoost, Histogram-based gradient boosting classifiers and LightGBM.

Slides : https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1c89f4ZRU6kQPybWpoO5v_lphAqqnPPfPEAkfVli85iM/edit?usp=sharing

Repository: https://github.com/hsma-programme/h6_4e_boosted_trees

HSMA Website : https://sites.google.com/nihr.ac.uk/hsma

videos.title: (HSMA 6 Day 12) 4E Part 2/2 - Predicting Numeric Values with Tree-based Algorithms + OneHot encoding
videos.description:
In this session we take a look at how decision trees, random forests and boosted trees can also be used when you want to predict a numeric value instead of classifying a sample as a member of one group or another. 

We also touch on some key parts of data preprocessing so we can work with a new dataset of patient length of stay in the final exercise, covering how to OneHot encode categorical variables to make this data usable with machine learning libraries. 

Slides : https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1c89f4ZRU6kQPybWpoO5v_lphAqqnPPfPEAkfVli85iM/edit?usp=sharing

Repository: https://github.com/hsma-programme/h6_4e_boosted_trees

HSMA Website : https://sites.google.com/nihr.ac.uk/hsma

videos.title: (HSMA 6 Day 13) 4F Neural Networks
videos.description:
In this session we'll be looking at a subfield of AI that has dominated many of the big advancements in AI over the last few years - Deep Learning - as we introduce Neural Networks.  Then, this afternoon, Sammi will dive into the fascinating emerging world of explainable AI as a way to build understanding, confidence and trust in our machine learning models.

videos.title: (HSMA 6 Day 14) 4J - Optimising ML: Imputation, Feature Engineering & Selection, Hyperparameters
videos.description:
**Unfortunately the first 5 minutes or so of the lecture was not recorded**

Covering a range of ways to improve your model's performance, including:

- Missing Data Imputation with SimpleImputer and IterativeImputer

- Feature Selection with SequentialFeatureSelector (forward and backward selection) and SelectFromModel (feature importance selection with model coefficients or mean decrease in impurity)

- Feature Engineering

- Dataset Splits (train/test/validation, k-fold)

- Dealing with Imbalanced Datasets with model parameters

- Hyperparameter tuning with exhaustive gridsearch, randomised gridsearch, and the Optuna framework

Additional areas in the slides, but not covered in the video, are:
- ensemble models
- sklearn pipelines
- automatic model selection with the flaml library
- model calibration curves (reliability plots)

Slides: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1t6eS93gkFfGMlfJ86cVShAZ2vOhmP08TFVp8rcgTGyQ/edit?usp=sharing

Code Slides Only: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1BBCc5TVEhfAY98I6JLKrsObLLeVseAsxYZSrgve20uI/edit?usp=sharing

We'll look at some core concepts important for processing text data, and learn a few little neat things we can do with our data along the way, including wordclouds and a method for assessing the similarity of different bits of text.

Today we're going to be looking at the crucial importance of version control, and how we can use Git - a distributed version control system - to allow us to this.  We'll also look at how we can use Git interaction with GitHub to publish and work with repositories hosted online.

videos.title: HSMA 5 3A : Introduction to Discrete Event Simulation and 3B : SimPy for DES Part 1
videos.description:
In these sessions, we introduce the simulation modelling approach Discrete Event Simulation - a way of modelling queuing / pathway problems.  We then show you how to use the Python package SimPy to build simple but effective Discrete Event Simulation models.  We also talk about Python Generator Functions - a structure that is fundamental to SimPy.

Note - these introductory sessions show you how to build simple SimPy models using a non-Object Oriented structure.  However, viewers are strongly recommended to additionally view the subsequent lecture which will show you how to structure a SimPy model in an elegant Object Oriented framework.

Accompanying lecture materials can be found here : 
Session 3A : https://github.com/hsma5/3a_introduction_to_discrete_event_simulation
Session 3B :
https://github.com/hsma5/3b_simpy_part_1

videos.title: HSMA 5 3C : SimPy for Discrete Event Simulation Pt 2 & 7A : Introduction to AI and Machine Learning
videos.description:
In the first part of the video (session 3C) we look at how we can make our SimPy models more elegant by structuring them in an Object-Oriented way.  We also look at how we can model entities having different priorities in a queue so that we use priorities to determine the next entity to be seen, and we look at how we can model unavailability of resources.

In the second part of the video (session 7A) we take out first tentative steps into the magical world of AI and Machine Learning.  We introduce some of the core concepts in these fields, with a focus on Supervised Machine Learning.  We then challenge our HSMAs to come up with an "algorithm" to determine the films Dan most enjoys, learning concepts such as features, labels, overfitting, underfitting, and performance metrics en route.

Accompanying lecture materials can be found here : 
Session 3C : https://github.com/hsma5/3c_simpy_part_2

videos.title: HSMA 5 7B : Ethics in AI and 7C : Machine Learning - Who Would Survive the Titanic?
videos.description:
In the first part of this video (7B) we discuss some of the important ethical considerations necessary when undertaking AI and Machine Learning projects.  We talk about issues around representation in our data, transparency of our models as well as the severe consequences that can happen when our AI models go wrong.

In the second part of this video (7C) we look at using the scikit-learn Python library to develop a simple Logistic Regression model to see if we can predict which passengers would survive the sinking of the Titanic.  We also look at how we can ensure our feature values fall on a consistent scale, look at how stratified k-fold validation can help us to improve model performance and we also look at Receiver Operator Characteristic (ROC) curves as a means of both assessing the potential performance of our model, as well as helping us to identify classification thresholds that will yield higher performance.

Accompanying lecture materials can be found here : 
Session 7B : https://github.com/hsma5/7b_ethics_in_ai
Session 7C : https://github.com/hsma5/7c_ml_who_would_survive_the_titanic

More information about the HSMA Programme can be found here : https://sites.google.com/nihr.ac.uk/hsma

Follow us on Twitter : @PenCHORD_UoE @drdanielchalk

videos.title: HSMA 5 7D : Introduction to Neural Networks and 7E : Synthetic Data
videos.description:
In the first part of this video (7D), we talk about Deep Learning and the magical world of Neural Networks.  These structures allow us to get high performance learning models for a wide range of problems, although they do come with a cost - that we lose a little bit in terms of model explainability (at least "out of the box").

In the second part of this video (7E), we question whether anything is real as we delve into the world of Synthetic Data - methods that allow us to create fake data that can be used either instead of real data, or to augment our data where we don't have enough examples for a particular classification for our machine learning model.  We talk briefly about a few different approaches, but then work through the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) approach.

Accompanying lecture materials can be found here : 
Session 7D : https://github.com/hsma5/7d_introduction_to_neural_networks

videos.title: HSMA 5 8A : Intro to Natural Language Processing and 8B : Named Entity Recognition & Word Clouds
videos.description:
IMPORTANT NOTE - there is an error in the teaching in this video which has since been corrected.  Specifically, some of the named entities that I suggested should have been picked up as named entities in Exercise 1 should not have been - "bread" and "milk" are not named entities as they are not identified with a proper name (unless we are referring to a particular brand of bread or milk).  Similarly, whilst "Discrete Event Simulation" counts as a named entity (as it has a proper name), "bread making" and "cookery" would not count.  Similarly, I have removed "woodwork" as an example in one of the teaching slides.  The materials in the links below (including the exercise solutions) have been corrected.

In the first part of this video (8A), we introduce Natural Language Processing as a means of automating the extraction of information from unstructured / free-text data.  We talk about Named Entity Recognition in particular, and explore common NLP concepts such as POS-tagging and parsing.

In the second part of this video (8B), we talk about how the FOSS Package SpaCy uses Transformers at its core.  We discuss how Transformers work in a broad sense, and talk about concepts such as Attention and Context.  We then go hands-on with SpaCy to undertake some Named Entity Recognition.  We also demonstrate use of the WordCloud library for generating word clouds from our text data.

Accompanying lecture materials can be found here : 
Session 8A : https://github.com/hsma5/8a_introduction_to_natural_language_processing
Session 8B : https://github.com/hsma5/8b_named_entity_recognition_and_word_clouds

More information about the HSMA Programme can be found here : https://sites.google.com/nihr.ac.uk/hsma

Follow us on Twitter : @PenCHORD_UoE

videos.title: HSMA 5 8C : Sentiment Analysis and 6A : Cellular Automata
videos.description:
In the first part of this video (8C) we revisit our old friend Neural Networks to see if we can apply the same principles to automatically predict the sentiment of a piece of text.  But because we're  dealing with text data, we'll need to look at the concepts of Standardisation and Vectorisation to get our text data Neural Network-ready.  We also look at using a handy Keras method that allows us to easily read in text files from different directories representing different classifications for our training.  We also talk a little bit about the field of Aspect-Level Sentiment Analysis, and Noun Chunks.

In the second part of this video (6A), we begin our journey into modelling behaviour by dipping our toes into the world of Cellular Automata - the purist distillation of Agent Based Simulation.  We jump in our oscillating spaceships, take part in a battle from Star Wars, avoid getting eaten by a Pulsar and journey to the Edge of Chaos and back again as we discover that the answer to life, the universe and everything is perhaps not 42, but the pattern on the cone snail Conus textile.  We also explore some potential application areas for this abstract modelling approach.

Accompanying lecture materials can be found here : 
Session 8C : https://github.com/hsma5/8c_sentiment_analysis
Session 6A : https://github.com/hsma5/6a_cellular_automata

More information about the HSMA Programme can be found here : https://sites.google.com/nihr.ac.uk/hsma

Follow us on Twitter : @PenCHORD_UoE

In this video, we walk through some code to develop a simple Agent Based Simulation to model the spread of a disease using the Python package MESA.  We talk about the concepts of Agent Based Simulation and how it can be used to model behaviour.  We then look at how MESA is structured, begin developing a simple model and see and how we can use MESA's server-based capabilities to visualise our models.

videos.title: HSMA 5 4B : System Dynamics and 2C : Patient and Public Involvement in Research
videos.description:
In the first part of this video (4B), we introduce you to the world of System Dynamics.  We look at how we can explore the influential dynamics within a system to try and understand something more about how the system works, and whether there are intrinsic problems within the structure of a system.  We use a lovely online piece of software called InsightMaker to do this - it's completely free and just requires you to register for a free account.  And the good news for those who need a break from coding - there's no Python (or any other language) needed, it's all drag and drop!

In the second part of this video (2C), our guest lecturers Georgia Jenkins, Lauren Asare and Leon Farmer talk about Patient and Public Involvement in Research - what it is, why it's important and the practicalities of involving patients and public in your research.

Accompanying lecture materials can be found here :

In this video, we introduce some of the core concepts of Reinforcement Learning by using the 80s cult-classic UK TV series Treasure Hunt as our inspiration.  We talk about the fundamental principles of Reinforcement Learning, the exploration / exploitation dilemma, multi-armed bandit problems and a Linear Operator Learning Rule.  We also touch on Deep Q Reinforcement Learning as an extension to the core principles which incorporates Neural Networks, and take some time to think about potential application areas for these methods.

videos.title: HSMA 5 2B : Principles of FOSS and Version Control using Git
videos.description:
In this video, we introduce viewers to the world of version control using Git and collaborative open source development using GitHub.  First, we talk about the importance of FOSS and Open Science.  We talk a bit about the history of FOSS, as well as reminisce about the good old days of computing, when a "high resolution display" meant that you tuned your TV into a slightly less fuzzy picture.

Then we move onto the meat of the session - introducing you to version control, and specifically, Git.  We'll talk about why version control is so important using an example from Father Ted, and show you the basics of Git, before giving you a chance to have a go at using Git yourselves.

Finally we explore the world of GitHub as an online sharing and repository platform, and how Git integrates with GitHub.  You'll have a chance to play with Git integration with GitHub, and hear a funny story about what happened when I wrote this training.  We draw our inspiration for the GitHub training from The Chuckle Brothers.

Accompanying lecture materials can be found here : 
Session 2B : https://github.com/hsma5/2b_principles_of_foss_and_version_control

In this Sesame Street-themed Masterclass session, we provide a beginner's introduction to the world of BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) for Natural Language Processing - a model published in 2018 that has transformed the landscape of NLP.  We provide a simple explanation of how BERT works using classic UK game shows for inspiration, and look at some hands-on code which fine tunes a BERT model for sentiment analysis of movie reviews.
